Relatively drier air upstream associated with a ridge will move over
the region tonight, so isolated showers will return through the 
middle of next week. A trade-wind surge will prevail for majority of
the forecast period as winds slightly reinforce over the coming 
days. East to northeast winds of 10 to 15 mph tonight will quickly 
increase to 15 to 20 mph with gusts up to 30 mph afterwards, similar 
to what was observed by METARs today. Towards the end of next week, a
wetter pattern associated with a potential tropical disturbance is 
forecast, but much can change this far out. Drought concerns are 
increasingly relevant, especially now that Guam and Rota are 
considered abnormally dry (D0) by the U.S. Drought Monitor. Residents
should prepare to take advantage of potential rain next week to 
mitigate early drought conditions.

Marine...
Combined seas of 5 to 7 feet will increase a foot or two beginning 
Sunday as the trade swell builds. This may also pose a high rip 
current risk to east-facing reefs. Model guidance has severely 
undermined the trade-wind surge today as METARs observed moderate to 
fresh trade winds with up to near-gale gusts over land and 
scatterometry showed 15 to 20 knots with a swath of 25 knots in the
western coastal waters. Model guidance indicates the trade winds to
slightly increase, and noting its current low bias, a Small Craft 
Advisory was issued earlier this afternoon, likely lasting through 
the weekend.

Fire weather...
The Keech-Bryam Drought Index (KBDI) is currently 563, indicating a 
high fire danger. As of 4 PM ChST, rainfall at the airport was 0.04 
inches, and with a lack of notable rainfall expected tonight, high 
fire danger is expected to continue. Trade winds may slightly 
strengthen, but could remain below Red Flag criteria. Regardless, 
fire weather is not expected to let up any time soon, so folks are 
urged to monitor any outdoor-related activities that involve a spark 
or flames, as elevated conditions are ongoing.

Eastern Micronesia...
Weather in eastern Micronesia is being affected by a Near-Equatorial
Trough (NET) and trade-wind surge. The trough lies south of both 
Pohnpei and Majuro, and will gradually move farther south, so it is 
affecting just Kosrae. Kosrae can look for numerous showers tonight 
and scattered showers Saturday through Wednesday. Meanwhile, Majuro 
will have isolated coverage through the entire period with the 
possible exception of Monday when showers could tick up one notch. 
Pohnpei will have isolated showers tonight, then scattered Saturday 
through Monday, then return to isolated. The trade-wind surge will be
pushing little troughs through to make that happen.

The other effect of the trade-wind surge will be increased winds,
which are producing sea conditions hazardous to small craft at
Pohnpei coastal waters, and hazardous surf along north and east
facing reefs of Kosrae. As such, a Small Craft Advisory has been
issued for Pohnpei, and a High Surf Advisory for Kosrae. A High Surf
Advisory is currently not needed at Pohnpei because it's mostly east
swell energy, and their east criteria are 12 feet. However, the 
north criteria is really close, so retained the headline about 
elevated surf, and a High Surf Advisory may yet be needed later. 
Kosrae doesn't really need to be in the Small Craft Advisory because 
they're south of the trade-wind surge, so wind speeds are lower, 
they're just getting swell. Their east facing surf advisory criteria 
is only 8 feet, so that's why they're getting an advisory. The north 
facing reefs at Kosrae are marginal at best. Since we were putting 
out an advisory for east facing reefs anyway though, it made sense to
throw in the north facing reefs.

Western Micronesia...
The Near-Equatorial Trough (NET) and embedded broad surface trough 
remain the dominant features bringing weather to western Micronesia. 
The surface trough will bring peak shower and thunder potential to 
Yap, with near gale-force gusts carried by heavier showers possible 
tonight, followed by slowly improving conditions thereafter as the 
trough moves away to the west-southwest and brings on-and-off showers
and thunderstorms to Palau Sunday and Sunday night. Weather will 
then improve steadily at both islands, with isolated to low-end 
scattered showers expected for much of next week. Mostly dry 
conditions are expected to continue across much of eastern Yap State 
as diffusive flow moves in from the northeast, likely increasing 
water stress across the atolls over the coming weeks as we are 
heading into a long period of drier conditions across the region.

Meanwhile at Chuuk, diffusive northeasterlies have ensued, bringing 
fresh to strong winds that are producing sea conditions hazardous to 
small craft; as such, a Small Craft Advisory is in effect for tonight
in Chuuk waters. Otherwise, mostly dry conditions are expected at 
Chuuk for at least the next several days.
